newsitem.title: UK: Eramet sees nickel balanced in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Eramet sees nickel balanced in 1996/97.

text.p: Supply and demand in the Western world nickel market is likely to be roughly balanced in 1996 and 1997, according to Yves Rambaud, chairman of French nickel group Eramet.

"The (nickel) market was more or less balanced in the first half of the year, and we think it it will be for the whole year," Rambaud said in a presentation to the Association of Mining Analysts on Thursday.
"For 1997...we have the feeling that the production of stainless steel will rise," he said.
Stainless steel accounts for around two-thirds of nickel consumption, and slower stainless steel production in 1996 has hit primary nickel demand.
"We are told by our customers that they think they are going to raise their production as soon as they achieve a better price," Rambaud said.
"The nickel market will be very close to a balanced market," he added.
He said stock levels were reduced to "more or less normal levels" by the end of 1995, after 100,000 tonnes of inventories were worked off during that year.
Exports to the Western world from Russia were likely to remain stable over the medium term.
"For 1996 we have the feeling that new exports (from Russia) are in line with last year and we don't see any reason for a higher figure in 1997," Rambaud said.
He did not give specific tonnages, but in May he said 1996 exports from Russia may be slightly above 150,000 tonnes.
Rambaud played down market rumours of sizeable off-market stocks of uncut nickel being held in Europe.
Traders and analysts had spoken of tonnages peaking between 20,000 and 40,000 tonnes.
Some of the nickel arriving in London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouses in recent months was material from these stocks being cut and delivered on to the LME, traders said.
"I am not so sure that tonnages of 20,000, 30,000 or 40,000 tonnes are really available somewhere in Europe," he said.
Rambaud said Eramet was looking to find new markets for its planned nickel output increases over the next few years.
The group was keen to secure demand for higher output before production from the giant Voisey Bay development in Canada comes on stream.
"I think we have the possibility to increase our sales and make the most of our investments before the real impact of new Canadian production is felt," he said.
"We are told their eventual production will be in the range of 100,000 to 130,000 tonnes," Rambaud said.
"But I don't think the production will be in the market for five, six, seven years. At that time we will have reached our level (of production) of 60,000 tonnes," he added.
Eramet is the Western world's third largest nickel producer.
In May Rambaud estimated global nickel consumption outside the former Soviet Union and China at 890,000 tonnes in 1995.
--Mike Collett-White, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8057
